name: lightsage
description: Turn prompt-run and eval evidence into prioritized, verifiable actions

interface.longDescription: Lightsage shows how AI assistants and coding agents talk about and use your product. With this plugin you can review your stored prompt runs to see where your brand is mentioned, recommended, and cited, diagnose eval runs that failed or regressed, and get a short list of prioritized actions backed by that evidence. It is for marketing, developer relations, and product teams who already use Lightsage. The plugin works on the Lightsage organization you choose when you sign in, and it needs a Lightsage account. It analyzes runs you already have; start new prompt runs from the Lightsage dashboard.
defaultPrompt: Review my recent prompt runs and recommend the three highest-impact actions.
Diagnose my latest failed eval and propose the smallest useful fix.
Which competitors do AI assistants recommend instead of us, and why?

positive.description: Confirm the plugin is connected and signed in to the right Lightsage organization
positive.prompt: Using Lightsage, check that I'm connected and tell me which organization this connection uses.
positive.expected_behavior: Confirms the connection is authenticated and states the organization ID and the permissions the connection has.

positive.description: See how visible the brand is in AI answers and how it compares with competitors
positive.prompt: Using Lightsage, how visible is my brand in AI answers, and how do we compare with competitors?
positive.expected_behavior: A summary with the recommendation score and visibility score, the trend over the period, a breakdown by AI platform, and a comparison against tracked competitors.

positive.description: Turn recent prompt runs into a short list of actions
positive.prompt: Using Lightsage, look at my recent prompt runs and give me the three most important things to fix.
positive.expected_behavior: Three prioritized actions, each tied to specific prompt runs, naming the prompt, the platform, and what the response said about the brand (mentions, position, citations).

positive.description: Find the best opportunities to improve AI visibility
positive.prompt: Using Lightsage, what are my best opportunities to improve AI visibility this month?
positive.expected_behavior: A ranked list of opportunities from the last 30 days, each with a short explanation of the gap and a suggested next step.

positive.description: Diagnose the most recent eval run
positive.prompt: Using Lightsage, what happened in my most recent eval run, and what should I change?
positive.expected_behavior: The latest eval run with its status, which attempts failed and why, and one specific change to try next. If nothing failed, it says so.

negative.description: The user asks about traditional search rankings and website traffic. Lightsage measures how AI assistants mention and cite a brand, not Google rankings or web analytics, so the plugin should not be used.
negative.prompt: What is my website's Google ranking for 'project management software', and how much traffic did I get last week?

negative.description: The user asks a general question about improving AI visibility, with no reference to their own Lightsage data. This is a general knowledge question and should be answered without calling the plugin.
negative.prompt: In general, what makes a brand more likely to be recommended by AI assistants?

negative.description: The user asks for help evaluating their own machine learning model. Lightsage evals test how coding agents use a company's product, not model training or accuracy, so the plugin should not be used.
negative.prompt: Help me evaluate the accuracy of my image classification model on my test set.

publication.release_notes: Removes the command-line skill from this package. The Lightsage MCP server no longer takes environment variables or MCP server headers in tool inputs; run settings come from the environments and MCP servers saved in the Lightsage app. Renames tools whose names did not match what they do, asks for confirmation before runs that use usage-based credits, and the privacy policy now covers AI assistant connections.
